claims.text: Replacing an EAM reference with an ML interatomic potential trained on ab initio liquid configurations will improve reference–target phase-space overlap.
Improved phase-space overlap will reduce mismatch along the thermodynamic-integration path.
The proposed method applies to multicomponent high-entropy alloys in both solid and liquid states near their high melting temperatures.
A neural-network or moment-tensor potential trained on ab initio liquid configurations can serve as the reference in free-energy calculations.
The proposed ML reference is applicable to complex refractory high-entropy alloys, including tungsten-based MPEAs.
The applicable temperature window extends from the melting region to approximately 10% above the melting temperature.
Liquid atomic configurations in this temperature range are highly diverse.
Training on a broad set of liquid atomic environments gives the ML potential a more complete representation of local bonding and interactions than EAM.
The ML potential captures many-body effects and nonlinearities that are inadequately represented by the EAM approach.
Fitting diverse ab initio liquid configurations enables the ML potential to reproduce the target system's detailed phase space.
Better reproduction of the ab initio liquid phase space increases overlap between the reference and target distributions.
Increased phase-space overlap reduces thermodynamic-integration errors relative to TOR-TILD's EAM references.
The ML reference will reduce free-energy pathway mismatch by approximately 50% or more relative to TOR-TILD EAM references.
Conventional TOR-TILD EAM references exhibit notable mismatch with ab initio liquid configurations.
The intervention is likely to be beneficial only for compositionally complex, multicomponent alloys near melting.
The intervention may be less effective for simpler systems or at temperatures well below melting.
The magnitude of improvement depends on training-set quality, scope, and generalization across relevant liquid configurations.
